reference.source: Bradley and Daroff Neurology in Clinical Practice
clinicalPearls: A highly variable adult-onset disorder that can present with dementia, episodic encephalopathy, parkinsonism, tremor, autonomic dysfunction or a peripheral neuropathy
Caused by a GGC trinucleotide repeat expansion in the NOTCH2NLC gene, with a growing spectrum of recognised phenotypes
The most characteristic imaging clue is a ribbon of high signal along the corticomedullary junction on diffusion-weighted imaging, corresponding to the subcortical U-fibres
Leukoencephalopathy and progressive white matter change are common as the disease advances
Skin biopsy showing eosinophilic, ubiquitin- and p62-positive intranuclear inclusions can support the diagnosis less invasively than brain biopsy
Episodes of encephalopathy with headache, altered consciousness or focal deficits may mimic stroke or encephalitis
Genetic testing for the NOTCH2NLC repeat expansion provides definitive confirmation
reference.pathophysiology: Neuronal intranuclear inclusion disease is a slowly progressive neurodegenerative disorder defined pathologically by eosinophilic hyaline intranuclear inclusions within neurones, glia and cells of many other tissues, including the skin. It is caused by an abnormal GGC repeat expansion in the NOTCH2NLC gene, which is thought to produce toxic effects through repeat-associated translation and sequestration of nuclear proteins into the inclusions. Widespread deposition affects the cerebral white matter, cortex, autonomic and peripheral nervous systems, accounting for the diverse clinical picture that ranges from dementia and encephalopathic episodes to neuropathy and autonomic failure.
additionalDifferentials: Leukoencephalopathies of other genetic or metabolic causes
Behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia or Alzheimer disease
Recurrent stroke or transient ischaemic attacks
Autoimmune or infective encephalitis during encephalopathic episodes
additionalInvestigations: MRI of the brain with diffusion-weighted imaging to detect the corticomedullary junction (U-fibre) ribbon
Skin biopsy to demonstrate p62- and ubiquitin-positive intranuclear inclusions
Genetic testing for the NOTCH2NLC GGC repeat expansion
Nerve conduction studies to characterise an associated peripheral neuropathy
Autonomic function testing where dysautonomia is prominent
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis to help exclude inflammatory and infective causes during encephalopathic episodes
redFlags: Acute encephalopathic episodes with reduced consciousness that may be mistaken for stroke or encephalitis
Progressive autonomic failure causing syncope or gastrointestinal and bladder dysfunction
Rapidly worsening cognition or recurrent seizures
New focal neurological deficits requiring exclusion of alternative acute pathology
reference.prognosis: The disorder is generally slowly progressive over years, though the course and rate vary widely between individuals; episodic encephalopathy, accumulating cognitive decline and autonomic involvement contribute to disability, and management is supportive.
pitfalls: Overlooking the diagnosis because the phenotype is so variable and may mimic many other disorders
Failing to review diffusion-weighted imaging for the characteristic subcortical ribbon
Not pursuing skin biopsy or NOTCH2NLC testing when the imaging pattern is suggestive
Attributing encephalopathic episodes solely to stroke or infection without considering NIID
references: Bradley and Daroff Neurology in Clinical Practice
Adams and Victor's Principles of Neurology
management: No disease-modifying therapy exists, so management is supportive and tailored to the individual's dominant manifestations
Manage encephalopathic episodes supportively with hydration and symptomatic care while excluding the stroke and encephalitis they may mimic
Treat parkinsonism with a trial of levodopa and manage tremor with appropriate agents where these features dominate
Manage dysautonomia, treating orthostatic hypotension, neurogenic bladder and gastrointestinal dysmotility
Provide neuropathic-pain treatment and rehabilitation for the associated peripheral neuropathy
Offer cognitive assessment, dementia support and caregiver input for progressive cognitive decline
Offer genetic counselling for the NOTCH2NLC GGC repeat expansion and consider family assessment given autosomal dominant inheritance in familial cases
